MINUTES OF A SPECIAL AND REGULAR MEETINGS OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
April 15, 2013

6:30 P.M. – CLOSED SESSION - SPECIAL MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

  A special meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 6:30 p.m., on Monday,
  April 15, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

  Mayor Estrada led the salute to the flag.

  c. Roll Call

  Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
  COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present
  were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, and Assistant
  City Clerk Shumway.

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AT 6:31 P.M.

  CLOSED SESSION

3.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to Government Code §54957
  Title: City Manager

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION AT 6:55 P.M.

4.  ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

City Attorney Hogin made an announcement during the Regular City Council meeting, after Item
#6, that City Council convened to closed session at 6:31 p.m., and that there was one item on
the agenda, which was discussed, but no reportable action was taken.

ADJOURN TO REGULAR MEETING

  Page 1
 7:00 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL

5.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, April
15, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Mayor Estrada led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

6.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

7.  SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada proclaimed Monday, April 22, 2013, as “Arbor Day / Looking Good Lomita Day.”

Mayor Estrada and the City Council presented a certificate of appointment to Ken Blackwood
(Parks and Recreation Commission).

Ken Blackwood presented the City with a $300.00 check from the Lions Club for Arbor Day
celebration.

Presentation by Calmet Services Inc., relating to solid waste and recycling services
provided to city residents and businesses.

J.B. D'Souza, CalMet Services Representative, provided an overview of Calmet Services’ recent
efforts in Lomita, including the replacement of trash containers in 2010, with new, more
aesthetically pleasing containers that are more convenient for residents. Ms. D’Souza also
stated that recycling in Lomita is increasing, while the amount of trash is decreasing. Finally,
Ms. D’Souza complimented City staff for their excellent outreach efforts regarding the mandatory
commercial recycling program.

  Page 2
 Page 3
 8.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the Cypress Water Production Facility
(CWPF) began operations on April 5, 2013, which included filling the tank to operational
capacity. The distribution of blended water also began on April 5, 2013, at a ratio of 70%/30%,
Metropolitan Water District (MWD) water to well water, respectively. According to City Manager
Rock, the TDS levels of the effluent water leaving CWPF ranges from 580 to 590 mg/l, for an
average of 587 mg/l, which is within the targeted range of 500 to 750 mg/l for TDS, and that the
hardness levels in the distribution system are within the targeted range of 180 to 250 mg/l, with
an approximate average of 226 mg/l. City Manager Rock also added that methane in the
reservoir effluent is being removed via aeration, and that the methane levels remain low and
consistent with low historical levels. After aeration, the methane levels in the reservoir effluent
remain negligible, between 0.21 to 0.34 mg/l, which at this low concentration pose no health or
safety risks; City Manager Rock also stated that staff continues to monitor methane daily, and
sampling is consistent with the requirements of the Department of Public Health. City Manager
Rock added that staff is looking to receive a permanent permit, but is currently collecting more
data to support its case. Finally, City Manager Rock stated that only nine complaints, related
mostly to odor and chlorine, had been received by staff.

Councilmember Gazeley expressed his concern with the potential shortage of water, and asked
staff to carefully watch water quality, especially during the summertime, as MWD water has had
algae bloom issues in the past. Public Words Director Damasse responded that staff is
constantly monitoring water quality.

9.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Savidan stated that only nine complaints out of 9,000 water users/customers is
good, and added that the City needs to continue with water blending. Furthermore,
Councilmember Savidan stated that he visited the CWPF, and informed those in attendance that
staff is taking the safety of residents seriously, and is working diligently to provide safe drinking
water.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that the first Community Emergency Response Team (CERT)
class took place on Saturday, April 13, 2013, with the other two classes scheduled for Saturday,
April 20, 2013, and Saturday, April 27, 2013; Councilmember Sanchez invited all interested
residents to attend. In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s question on whether discussion
regarding unfunded pension liabilities could be placed on a future agenda, Mayor Estrada
responded that the topic will be part of the upcoming budget discussion for Fiscal Year 2013-
2014.

Councilmember Traina reported that he received three complaints related to water odor since
April 1, 2013.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended a meeting of the Southern California
Association of Governments, and that one of the discussions was on Property Assessed Clean
Energy (PACE) programs, which allow local governments to offer sustainable energy project
loans to eligible property owners. Councilmember Gazeley asked staff to look into how Lomita
could possibly participate in the PACE program.

  Page 4
 10. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Judy Daily, Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited everyone to the Lomita
Chamber's Breakfast on Friday, April 19, 2013, from 7:30 a.m. to 9 a.m., at which California
State Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi will be a speaker. Ms. Daily also invited everyone to the
9th Annual Golden Apple Awards Dinner, which will be held on Thursday, May 9, 2013, from 6:00
p.m. to 9:00 p.m., where the keynote speaker will be Dr. Richard Vladovic.

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, stated that she noticed both a residue and sulfur odor since
the beginning of water blending.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, complimented Calmet Service drivers for their exceptional
service. Mr. Friedrich also inquired as to whether the complaints received regarding water
quality could be posted on the City’s website.

11. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Gazeley
seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina requested discussion regarding Item 11.D. In
response to Councilmember Traina’s question whether Item 11.D. was related to the storm drain
screens previously discussed at a City Council meeting, Assistant City Manager Sugano stated
that that particular issue was not related to the storm drain screens issues, which will be brought
back to City Council at a future meeting. The motion carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on April
  1, 2013, and the Regular City Council Meeting held on April 1, 2013. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands.

  d. Consider authorizing the Mayor to sign a Letter to Undersecretary Burns of the Cal EPA
  Requesting a Stay of the MS4 Permit. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  e. Report recommending Arbor Day / Looking Good Lomita Day to be held on April 22, 2013.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING:

12. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF AN ORDINANCE PERTAINING TO LOT LINE
  ADJUSTMENTS.

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that staff initiated a text amendment to the Lomita
Municipal Code, proposing elimination of the requirement for a lot line adjustment to be no more
than 25 feet from the original lot line. Assistant City Manager Sugano went on to explain the
conditions when lot line adjustments could be made, and recommended eliminating the 25 foot
arbitrary requirement, and for the City to establish its own zoning regulations specific to lot line
adjustments.

  Page 5
 City Attorney Hogin explained that parcel lot lines are heavily regulated by the State of
California, with the Subdivision Map Act specifically defining how parcels can be changed.
According to City Attorney Hogin, instead of changing or redoing a map, lot line adjustments are
a shortcut that allows for existing lot changes within set requirements. City Attorney Hogin
added that no court has looked into this issue yet, so it would be safe to either adopt the
ordinance tonight or postpone adoption to see if there is a conflict.

Discussion followed on what the average footage requested was for lot line adjustments, and
how many lot line adjustments had been requested. Assistant City Manager Sugano responded
to the discussion that the average lot line adjustment requested was between five and ten feet,
and that the City has only received seven such applications since 2000.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing. There was no public input. Mayor Estrada closed
public input.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to table the item to a date uncertain. Councilmember Gazeley
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

13. DISCUSSION OF APPEAL PROCEDURES FOR PLANNING COMMISSION DECISIONS

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that based on City Council’s last discussion regarding
appeal procedures for Planning Commission decisions, staff is recommending direction be
given to prepare an ordinance to include Option #5 (for City Council to be able to request an
appeal/review of Planning Commission decisions) and Option #8 (increasing the appeal period
from 15 to 21 days). Councilmember Traina moved to give staff direction to prepare an
ordinance consistent with Option #5 and Option #8. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:44 p.m., in memory of Kimberly Bergan, Bobby Cantrell, and the victims
killed at the Boston Marathon.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
